newsitem.title: CROATIA: Serbs throw bricks at HDZ members in rebel enclave.
newsitem.headline: Serbs throw bricks at HDZ members in rebel enclave.

text.p: Hundreds of angry Serbs attacked delegates from Croatia's ruling party who had to be rescued by U.N. peacekeepers while trying to campaign in Eastern Slavonia on Monday.

U.N. official Douglas Coffman told Reuters the Croatian Democratic party or HDZ held a press conference in a hotel in the town of Vukovar to present candidates who will run in the Serb enclave during nation-wide local elections on April 13.
The vote for county and municipal bodies will be the first in independent Croatia held on all of its sovereign territory, including Eastern Slavonia which is due to revert to Croatian rule soon.

Eastern Slavonia was one of three parts of Croatia in which local Serbs rebelled against the break-up of the old Yugoslav federation in 1991. It held out longest against government forces and is now under the control of 5,000 U.N. peacekeepers.
Coffman said the HDZ members were first confronted by a small group of middle-aged women but the demonstration grew until there were "hundreds of protesters".
"On their way out (of the hotel) HDZ activists and accompanying Croatian journalists were hit by a barrage of eggs and bricks, but nobody sustained any serious injuries, only bruises," Coffman said.
"They had to be evacuated by Russian (peacekeepers) in armoured personal carriers to the U.N. bases and then they were escorted out of the region (to Croatian government territory)," he said.
U.N. officials are concerned that many Serbs may leave Eastern Slavonia before Zagreb's control is restored, fearing reprisals or refusing to live under Croatian rule.
